title: Statutory Grievance & Takedown Notice to Intermediary under Information Technology Act, 2000 & IT Rules, 2021
whenToUse: Use when serving a mandatory statutory notice to an intermediary (social media platform, search engine, web host) demanding takedown of defamatory, infringing, or voyeuristic content within statutory timelines.
variantComparisonNote: Statutory takedown notice to trigger loss of intermediary safe harbour under Section 79. Distinct from criminal police complaint.
youWillNeed: Specific URLs of infringing content, screenshots with timestamp, proof of identity / copyright ownership, Section 63 BSA certificate.
legalBasis: Section 79(3)(b) Information Technology Act, 2000; Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (Rules 3(1)(b) & 3(2)); Shreya Singhal v. UOI (2015).
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Exact URL links and precise location of the offensive/unlawful content
Clear demonstration that content violates Rule 3(1)(b) of IT Rules, 2021
Statutory timeline demand: 24 hours for voyeuristic/impersonation content, 36 hours for other violations
Warning of loss of safe harbour immunity under Section 79(1) upon failure to expeditiously remove

aiBlocks.title: Statutory Due Diligence Obligations under IT Rules
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Demonstrate strict statutory obligations under Rule 3(1)(b) and 3(2) of IT Rules, 2021 requiring proactive disabled access within statutory timeframes.

aiBlocks.title: Demand for Takedown & Forfeiture of Safe Harbour
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Demand removal within 24/36 hours, preservation of computer records under Rule 3(1)(h), and warning of civil and criminal liability with forfeiture of Section 79 safe harbour.
